Efficacy and Safety of Pelacarsen in Black/African American and Hispanic Participants with Elevated Lipoprotein(a) and Established Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: The Randomized Controlled Lp(a)FRONTIERS EXPANSION Study.
items.abstract: Background: Black and Hispanic individuals may experience a disproportionate burden of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]-associated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk, and ASCVD-related mortality, yet remain underrepresented in cardiovascular (CV) clinical trials. Efficacy and safety data on Lp(a)-targeted therapies in these populations are limited. Methods: Lp(a)FRONTIERS EXPANSION was a randomized, double-blind, phase 3b, placebo-controlled trial assessing the efficacy and safety of pelacarsen, an Lp(a)-targeted therapy, in US Black/African American and Hispanic participants with elevated Lp(a) (≥125 nmol/L) and ASCVD. Eligible adults were randomized 2:1 to monthly subcutaneous pelacarsen 80 mg or placebo for 12 months, followed by 16 weeks of safety follow-up. Enrollment spanned May 2024-March 2025. The primary endpoint was change in log-transformed Lp(a) from baseline at Week 52, analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures. Results: Overall, 423 participants were randomized, with 422 analyzed (282 to pelacarsen; 140 to placebo). The population comprised 64.5% (n=272) Black/non-Hispanic, 30.1% (n=127) nonBlack/Hispanic, and 5.5% (n=23) Black/Hispanic. Trial completion rates were 90.1% and 91.4% for pelacarsen and placebo groups, respectively; median (Q1, Q3) baseline Lp(a) levels were 232.70 nmol/L (165.80, 301.50) and 219.25 nmol/L (166.95, 293.65). Geometric mean ratio (GMR) of Lp(a) to baseline at Week 52 was 0.14 (95% CI: 0.12, 0.16) with pelacarsen and 0.98 (95% CI: 0.80, 1.20) with placebo; GMR between groups (pelacarsen/placebo) was 0.14 (95% CI: 0.11, 0.18; P Conclusions: This study is the first to demonstrate robust Lp(a) lowering with pelacarsen, which was generally well tolerated, in US Black/African American and Hispanic participants, populations disproportionately impacted by Lp(a)-associated CV risk. items.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Anti-GABA A Receptor Encephalitis Presenting as Fulminant Hemicerebellitis in a 5-Year-Old Girl.
items.abstract: A previously healthy 5-year-old girl presented with several days of fever/malaise followed by acute neurologic decline. Head CT demonstrated fulminant right cerebellitis with edema and fourth-ventricle effacement concerning for impending herniation. She underwent emergent posterior fossa decompression. CSF showed mild pleocytosis, and MRI revealed right cerebellar nonenhancing T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintense lesions with evolving supratentorial cortical involvement. Despite empiric antimicrobials and initial immunotherapy (high-dose IV methylprednisolone and tocilizumab followed by IV immunoglobulin/plasma exchange), she developed progressive neuroinflammation with new seizures and markedly elevated CSF IL-6, prompting escalation to additional IL-6-directed therapy with tocilizumab and rescue intrathecal dexamethasone. She subsequently stabilized with radiographic improvement and meaningful neurologic recovery. Expanded antibody testing later confirmed anti-GABA A receptor (anti-GABA A R) encephalitis. This case highlights fulminant cerebellitis as a life-threatening presentation of anti-GABA A R encephalitis and underscores the importance of early posterior fossa decompression, parallel diagnostic evaluation (including expanded antibody panels), and coordinated, time-sensitive immunotherapy escalation in select critically ill presentations.

items.title: Decision-Making About Respiratory Syncytial Virus Immunization for Infants: Qualitative Interview Study.
items.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of infant hospitalization in the United States. Although maternal RSV vaccination and infant RSV monoclonal antibody products are recommended to protect infants during their first RSV season, uptake has remained modest. Understanding how pregnant individuals make decisions about these products is critical for informing strategies that support timely immunization. The study aimed to examine the behavioral and social drivers shaping decisions regarding RSV vaccination during pregnancy and infant RSV monoclonal antibody immunization among pregnant individuals in the United States. We conducted an exploratory qualitative study from a relativist epistemological perspective, using semistructured interviews with 12 pregnant and postpartum adults recruited across the United States between October 2024 and May 2025. Participants were purposively sampled to include individuals with positive, uncertain, and negative intentions toward RSV vaccination. Interviews were guided by the World Health Organization's behavioral and social drivers of vaccination framework and analyzed using a framework analysis approach. Screening survey data were summarized descriptively to characterize participant immunization intentions and contextualize the qualitative findings. RSV immunization decisions reflected interacting behavioral, emotional, social, and practical influences rather than attitudes alone. Participants with positive vaccination intentions described greater trust in medical expertise, confidence in vaccination, and personal or professional experience with RSV illness. Those with unsure or negative intentions emphasized the novelty of RSV vaccines, concerns about safety and long-term effects, and greater reliance on clinician recommendations and peer experiences when making decisions. Across intention groups, participants expressed a preference for receiving protection during pregnancy rather than after birth but reported uncertainty related to vaccine availability, timing within the 32- to 36-week eligibility window, and inconsistent integration into prenatal care. Participants consistently identified trusted clinician communication, opportunities for early discussion, and access to clear educational materials as important influences on decision-making. Decisions regarding RSV immunization during pregnancy are shaped by interconnected motivational, interpersonal, and structural factors. Integrating education on RSV and RSV immunization options earlier in prenatal care, strengthening clinician recommendations, and reducing logistical barriers to maternal vaccination may improve informed decision-making and timely uptake of infant RSV protection.

items.title: Intractable Nausea and Vomiting: A Key Feature of Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Area postrema syndrome (APS) can present with hiccups, nausea, or vomiting as a neurological presentation of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD). However, the diagnosis may be delayed and can result in neurological sequelae that include optic neuritis or myelitis. This report describes the case of a 22-year-old woman with intractable nausea, vomiting, and hiccups due to APS as a clinical manifestation of NMOSD. CASE REPORT A 22-year-old woman presented with a 5-week history of nausea, vomiting, and hiccups. After 3 emergency department visits, a first admission attributed her symptoms to gastroparesis on the basis of a gastric emptying study showing delayed emptying. Symptoms persisted despite antiemetic and prokinetic therapy, and she was readmitted 2 weeks later with new persistent hiccups and progressive bilateral upper-limb weakness. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the head and cervical spine demonstrated an expansile T2-hyperintense lesion of the dorsal lower medulla and upper cervical cord. Given a high suspicion for a demyelinating attack, plasma exchange and high-dose intravenous corticosteroids were started before serology results returned. Serum aquaporin-4 immunoglobulin G (AQP4-IgG) was subsequently positive, establishing AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD. Motor function improved after 7 plasma exchange sessions and rehabilitation, and she regained ambulation with a walker. CONCLUSIONS This report describes APS as the initial manifestation of NMOSD in a young woman whose intractable nausea, vomiting, and hiccups were first attributed to gastroparesis. NMOSD should be considered when unexplained nausea, vomiting, or hiccups persist beyond 48 hours, since prompt MRI and AQP4-IgG testing allow immunotherapy to begin without delay.

items.title: A Diagnostic Pitfall on 18F-FDG PET/CT: Transient Vertebral FDG Uptake During Immunotherapy.
items.abstract: An 80-year-old man with poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT for initial staging and treatment response assessment following pembrolizumab therapy. Follow-up PET/CT demonstrated a new FDG-avid focus within the T3 vertebral body without a corresponding CT abnormality. Subsequent contrast-enhanced MRI revealed no structural correlate at the site of uptake. A repeat PET/CT performed 3 months later showed complete resolution of the vertebral lesion without additional treatment. The imaging findings favored transient immune-related inflammatory uptake or a pseudoprogression-like phenomenon rather than true osseous metastasis.

items.title: Beyond immune suppression: Revisiting adenosine A2A receptor biology in CD8 + T-cell differentiation, metabolic fitness and cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Extracellular adenosine is a major immunosuppressive metabolite of the tumor microenvironment and a key barrier to anti-tumor immunity. Generated from ATP by the ectonucleotidases CD39 and CD73, it signals mainly through the high-affinity A2A adenosine receptor (A2AR). Although A2AR is regarded as an inhibitory immune checkpoint, recent work shows that its functions extend beyond immediate effector suppression to the regulation of metabolic fitness, mitochondrial homeostasis, and CD8 + T-cell differentiation. Notably, both sustained A2AR activation and complete receptor deficiency can drive terminal exhaustion through distinct mechanisms, and CD73 and extracellular adenosine are not biologically equivalent. Here we summarize adenosine signaling, the cell-specific roles of the A2AR axis, and the clinical development of A2AR-targeting immunotherapies. We identify the principal obstacles to therapeutic translation and advance biomarker-guided, calibrated modulation of A2AR signaling as a testable hypothesis rather than an established therapeutic principle, one that now requires comparative exposure-response and longitudinal intervention studies.

items.title: Structural basis of hypervariable region 1 dynamics on HCV envelope glycoproteins in immune evasion.
items.abstract: The hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) of the hepatitis C virus E1E2 glycoprotein plays a crucial role in immune evasion through rapid mutation and shielding of conserved neutralizing epitopes. Despite its important role, the structural properties of HVR1 remain poorly understood, particularly how its conformation influences shielding mechanisms and receptor recognition. To date in all published E1E2 or E2 structures, the C-terminal part of HVR1 (394 to 411) remains unresolved. Using neutralizing antibody (nAb) RM1-38, which targets C-terminal HVR1 (residues 399 to 409), we investigated the folding, positioning, flexibility, and shielding function of the RM1-38 epitope, or antigenic site 399 (AS399), on HVR1 by X-ray crystallography and negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM). The crystal structure of RM1-38 Fab with the HVR1 AS399 peptide, combined with mutagenesis analysis, delineated the molecular basis of its strain-specific recognition and neutralization. nsEM and competition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay revealed that HVR1 exhibits pronounced conformational flexibility even in the presence of other nAbs bound to E1E2. Virus neutralization assays using a combination of RM1-38 and broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) demonstrated antagonistic effects of RM1-38 with the bnAbs. Furthermore, RM1-38 reduced E1E2 binding to cells expressing the scavenger receptor SR-BI, an HVR1-dependent receptor, but did not affect binding to CD81 tetraspanin. Together, these findings support a model in which HVR1 functions as a dynamic shield, where its conformational plasticity contributes to both receptor engagement and evasion of humoral immunity in persistent infection.

items.title: Global Prognostic Impact of Substance Use in Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis.
items.abstract: Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) carries high short-term mortality. Although concomitant substance use is common in patients with AH, its impact on clinical outcomes remains unclear. We aimed to determine the prevalence of active substance use and evaluate its association with clinical outcomes in a large, multinational cohort of hospitalized patients with AH. We conducted a prospective, multicenter study across 38 centers in 13 countries (2015-2024). Adults meeting National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) criteria for AH were enrolled. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality stratified by substance use. Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were used to identify mortality predictors, with liver transplantation (LT) treated as a competing event. We included 814 patients, with a mean age of 49.5 ± 10.6 years, and 88.8% were male. Active cannabis and cocaine use were reported in 6.1% and 5.5%, respectively. Over follow-up, 210 patients (25.8%) died, and 35 (4.3%) underwent LT. In multivariable analysis, active cannabis use independently predicted higher mortality (sHR 2.49, 95% CI 1.52-4.09; p < 0.001), along with higher MELD scores and ACLF grades 2-3. Corticosteroid therapy (sHR 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.85; p = 0.007) and higher educational levels (sHR 0.34 and 0.31 for intermediate and highest categories, respectively) were associated with improved survival. Active substance use-particularly cannabis use-was independently associated with increased mortality in patients hospitalized with AH, even after adjusting for liver disease severity and accounting for transplantation as a competing event. These findings identify a behavioral dimension of AH severity and highlight the need to integrate addiction medicine and psychiatric care into hepatology practice to improve outcomes.

A Competency Assessment Tool for Liver Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Among Sonography Trainees: Development and Multicenter Validation Study.
items.abstract: Despite the increasing use of liver contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), no standardized, organ-specific tool exists for assessing trainees' cognitive competency. Existing instruments lack multidimensional evaluation and external validation, which limit training quality and patient safety. This study aims to develop and validate the CEUS Competency Assessment for the Liver (CCAL), a tool to standardize the evaluation of theoretical and cognitive skills in liver CEUS. This retrospective cohort study had four stages: (1) item generation from literature and guidelines, (2) 3 Delphi rounds (12/21, 57.1% female experts; mean age 51.0, SD 7.2 y) and cognitive testing (10 trainees) for content validity (>85% agreement) and clarity, (3) internal validation involving 100 sonography trainees (n=66, 66% assistant professors; n=27, 27% associate professors; n=7, 7% professors; n=70, 70% CEUS-naive) with 1 month or more of training at 4 hospitals (2018-2020), and (4) external validation on 579 sonography trainees (n=299, 51.6% assistant professors; n=183, 31.6% associate professors; n=97, 16.8% professors; n=439, 75.8% CEUS-naive) with 1 or more months of training at 25 multicenter sites (2018-2020). Primary outcomes were reliability (Cronbach α and Guttman split-half) and validity (exploratory factor analysis and item discrimination), while secondary outcomes included item difficulty distribution, pass rates, and between-group differences. The final CCAL comprised 74 items across 3 domains (demographics: 8, self-evaluation: 13, and objective questions: 53). Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach α=0.916 and Guttman split-half=0.908). Factor analysis confirmed a 3-factor structure explaining 74.6% of the cumulative variance. Item analysis showed a balanced difficulty distribution (35/53, 66.0% easy; 17/53, 32.1% moderate; 1/53, 1.9% difficult items). Scores varied significantly by CEUS training duration ( P F 2,576 =34.751, partial η²=0.108, 95% CI 0.069-0.147) and objective question ( F 2,576 =34.374, partial η²=0.107, 95% CI 0.068-0.146) scores than those with less than 3 months of training. Prior independent CEUS experience was also associated with higher scores on the self-evaluation ( t 577 =6.736, Cohen d =0.561, 95% CI 0.393-0.728; P t 577 =3.494, Cohen d =0.291, 95% CI 0.127-0.454; P =.001). Competency gaps were identified across specific competency domains: the pass rate ranged from 32.5% (188/579; image-guided intervention) to 81.3% (471/579; indications and contraindications). The CCAL is the first liver-specific CEUS competency tool integrating objective knowledge testing with structured self-evaluation. Unlike generic or simulation-based tests, it is organ-specific and validated across a large multicenter cohort, providing a multidimensional framework that identifies specific competency gaps, most notably in advanced image-guided procedures, beyond global pass/fail outcomes. The tool supports competency-based medical education through rigorous data-driven assessment, targeted curricular improvements, cross-institutional benchmarking, and informed training standards. It evaluates cognitive competence exclusively and should not replace procedural assessment in high-stakes decisions. International validation and the establishment of criterion-related and predictive validity are essential next steps.

items.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics define a C3-centred multicellular ecology in colorectal liver metastasis.
items.abstract: Colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) develops through malignant-cell plasticity and microenvironmental remodeling, yet the spatial principles by which epithelial, stromal, vascular and myeloid states assemble remain poorly defined. We integrated a 136,995-cell single-cell atlas, four spatial transcriptomic sections and bulk-cohort survival analysis. cNMF resolved three recurrent malignant programs-C1 Proliferative-biosynthetic, C2 AP-1 stress-inflammatory and C3 Secretory-invasive immune-like-which recurred across donors (with a rare, patient-associated tuft/chemosensory component in C3) and followed a pseudotime-associated C1-to-C2-to-C3 ordering rather than a demonstrated temporal progression. C3 cells, rare overall and of donor-dependent abundance, showed epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and invasive features, and in exploratory analyses their signature was associated with shorter recurrence-free survival. Continuous RGS1/CTSL programs captured macrophage heterogeneity more robustly than discrete subclusters. Spatial deconvolution revealed recurrent Fib-COL10A1-Endo-GJA5 proximity and variable C3 integration, with focal CTSL-program macrophage interfaces; MAPK and VEGF pathway activity was higher in C3-rich regions, although this association depended on how C3 was measured. An INHBA-CST6-LBH-FSTL3 score, which aggregates C3 and stromal expression, was associated with recurrence in TCGA, with partial external support in GSE39582 and no demonstrated gain over clinical variables. Virtual knockout of CST6 and LBH and LINCS screening prioritized MEK inhibition (PD-0325901) as a candidate for reversing the C3-associated transcriptional state; no target-engagement claim is made. Together, these findings define a spatially variable, C3-centred multicellular ecology in CRLM and provide a testable computational framework nominating recurrence-associated signatures and network-level candidates for experimental validation.

items.title: Long-Term Survival of Liver Transplantation in Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Insights From National Claims Data.
items.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading indication for liver transplantation (LT) in the United States. While post-transplant outcomes are well established, the relative survival benefit of LT compared to non-LT remains underdefined. Using Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database, we identified adults with ALD between 2017 and 2024. We used logistic regression to evaluate factors associated with LT, and Cox regression to compare survival between LT recipients and non-recipients. Among 373,025 patients with ALD, 3453 underwent LT. Female sex (adjusted OR = 0.805; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.750-0.866), African-American race (adjusted OR = 0.542; 95% CI: 0.462-0.636), older age, and non-liver comorbidities, and all types of metastatic cancer were associated with lower odds of LT; non-metastatic liver cancer, however, was associated with increased odds of LT (adjusted OR = 4.147; 95% CI: 3.659-4.699). The 8-year restricted mean survival time was 2600 days (~7.12 years) for LT recipients and 1799 days (~4.93 years) for nonrecipients. The median survival among deceased patients was 1000 days with LT vs. 355 days without LT. LT was associated with a lower adjusted mortality risk (HR, 0.365; 95% CI: 0.333-0.401). LT confers a substantial survival advantage for patients with ALD, beyond what is achieved without transplantation. However, significant sex and race-based disparities persist, underscoring the need for policy interventions to promote equitable access and optimized candidate selection.

items.title: Dual-Targeted Galactose-TPP Dendrimers Modulate Mitochondrial Function and Downstream Outcomes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains therapeutically challenging. Sorafenib, the standard first-line therapy for advanced HCC, suffers from poor aqueous solubility, non-specific biodistribution, dose-limiting toxicities, and the emergence of mitochondrial-mediated resistance. Here, we engineered a dual-targeted dendrimer nanoplatform that integrates hepatocyte-selective recognition with organelle-specific drug delivery. Galactose-functionalized Gal24 dendrimers were designed to engage the asialoglycoprotein receptor, while triphenylphosphonium enabled mitochondrial localization. Sorafenib was conjugated through CuAAC click chemistry to generate Gal24-TPP-Sora, which exhibited enhanced aqueous solubility, colloidal stability, and mitochondrial accumulation. In Hep3B cells, Gal24-TPP-Sora induced profound mitochondrial dysfunction, evidenced by elevated superoxide generation, ATP depletion, membrane depolarization, and enhanced apoptosis, accompanied by marked inhibition of proliferation, migration, and clonogenic survival. These effects surpassed free sorafenib and non-mitochondrial controls while preserving cytocompatibility and hemocompatibility. Collectively, this work establishes a precision nanotherapeutic strategy that couples receptor-mediated targeting with the mitochondrial intervention to potentiate sorafenib activity and overcome key therapeutic limitations in advanced HCC.

items.title: AI-Driven Discovery Pipeline Identifies Carvedilol as a Novel Partial Agonist of THRβ.
items.abstract: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRβ) is a key therapeutic target for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia, yet the discovery of structurally diverse agonists remains challenging. Here, we developed an AI-driven hierarchical drug discovery framework integrating graph neural network (GNN)-based virtual screening, structure-based modeling, and multilevel biological validation to accelerate THRβ agonist identification. The optimized GNN model outperformed conventional machine-learning approaches and enabled efficient prioritization of active compounds from an in-house library. Subsequent molecular docking and MM/GBSA rescoring identified Carvedilol as a high-confidence candidate. TR-FRET assays confirmed that Carvedilol acts as a partial THRβ agonist with preferential SRC2-2 coactivator recruitment, comparable to Resmetirom. Cellular assays further demonstrated that Carvedilol significantly reduced lipid accumulation and triglyceride levels and upregulated key metabolic regulators, including DIO1, ME1, and LDLR. Molecular dynamics and dcTMD analyses elucidated that Carvedilol is stabilized within the ligand-binding pocket through dominant hydrophobic interactions and specific hydrogen bonds with Thr273 and His435. Overall, this study repurposes Carvedilol as a structurally distinct THRβ agonist and validates an effective AI-guided strategy for nuclear receptor-targeted drug discovery.
